dct_description_sm: This project had two objectives, which were to map clam habitat and submerged shoreline features along the coastal waters of Broughton Channel, Baffin Island, NU. Submerged shore ridges and terraces in Broughton Channel were examined to understand their significance as indicators of past sea level and to map the palaeogeography of the channel. The mapping survey was complemented by underwater video camera surveys and sampling of the seabed to characterize the habitats for benthic organisms, especially clams, in the vicinity of Qikiqtarjuaq. The specific goals of this project were: 1) To characterize the modern and submerged shoreline features in order to understand their relation to historical and ongoing sea-level change; and 2) To assess the spatial variation in benthic invertebrate communities with relation to the seabed type and depths within a marine habitat mapping context. This research will help to constrain projections of sea-level rise for the region and contribute to a baseline dataset and possible future revival of the clam fishery.
dct_title_s: Coastal Seabed and Benthic Habitat Mapping of Broughton Channel, Qikiqtarjuaq, Nunavut
